To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the SDT intervention was successful in enhancing autonomy support and that this led to greater autonomous and competence motivation and smoking cessation in a sample of smokers who were relatively poor, undereducated, and not motivated to quit smoking.
the SDT intervention and process model were effective for promoting smoking cessation in a disadvantaged population.

a self-determination intervention for smoking cessation was effective in a low-income sample and that the intervention was effective because it increased autonomous motivation, competence, and cessation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the motivational and behavioral effects of autonomy-supportive and controlling social contexts in health care settings and the role of autonomy support and autonomy motivation in the internalization and implementation of health behaviors.
the motivational and behavioral processes by which autonomy support and competence support lead to smoking cessation.
the development and evaluation of a theoretically grounded intervention to promote smoking cessation in low-income populations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SDT intervention and process model for health behavior change was supported by the data and that it can be used to develop effective clinical interventions to motivate health behavior change.
the SDT intervention and process model was supported in a longitudinal randomized clinical trial of smokers.
the SDT process of internalization of autonomous and competence motivations was confirmed as the process through which autonomy support leads to smoking cessation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SDT intervention and process model were effective for motivating smoking cessation in a clinical trial with relatively disadvantaged patients.
the SDT model of motivation is applicable to smoking cessation and that perceived autonomy support is a critical determinant in the process of health behavior change.
SDT interventions are effective in improving smoking cessation in low-income smokers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
autonomy support and the SDT process of internalization are important to consider when developing smoking cessation treatments.
autonomy supportive interventions can help patients to achieve greater internalization of autonomous motivations and perceived competence.
autonomy support is a key ingredient of interventions that promote health behavior change.
